excerpt: The station was KXLP, 50 watts, and it reached just far enough to catch the edges of three counties before dissolving into static. Lena had taken the night shift because she didn't sleep anyway. She arrived at eleven, the parking lot gravel crunching under her boots, and sat in the dim glow of the board until dawn painted the blinds gold.

title: The Other Side
summary: Claire hadn't been swimming in eleven years. This was a decision she had made deliberately, the way you make decisions when you understand your own particular damage — not out of fear, but out of a kind of respect. You do not provoke the water. The water remembers.

title: The Question
summary: A quiet story about the questions we stop asking ourselves. A meditation on curiosity, time, and the weight of the unasked.
excerpt: The seminar met on the second floor of Hargrove Hall, in a room that smelled like chalk dust and old buildings and the particular quiet that accumulates in places where ideas have been exchanged for decades. title: The Seed Library at the End of May
summary: The Seed Library at the End of May — a short story about what we save, what we sow, and the harvests we never see coming.

title: The Weight of Summer Light
summary: The letter from the town clerk arrived on a Tuesday in April, three weeks after the last cold snap and two days after the forsythia in her neighbor's yard erupted into yellow so bright it looked like the bushes were on fire. Eleanor folded the envelope into thirds, then into sixths, and set it on the kitchen table, where it waited like a small white flag.
excerpt: The letter from the town clerk arrived on a Tuesday in April, three weeks after the last cold snap and two days after the forsythia in her neighbor's yard erupted into yellow so bright it looked like the bushes were on fire. Eleanor folded the envelope into thirds, then into sixths, and set it on the kitchen counter where it sat for the rest of the day like a small accusation.

title: They Walk Among Us
